claim: MAD1 Arg558His has been identified as a susceptibility factor for lung cancer.
source: Specifically, MAD1 Arg558His has been identified as a susceptibility factor for lung cancer Guo et al., 2010 and colorectal cancer (Zhong et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to Guo et al., 2010 and Zhong et al., 2015

claim: MAD1 allele carrying a p.Arg558His substitution may disrupt the interaction between MAD1 and MAD2.
source: Here, we found that MAD1 allele carrying a p.Arg558His substitution may disrupt the interaction between MAD1 and MAD2 (Figure 7c).
evidence: Molecular dynamics simulation results shown in Figure 7c

claim: The binding affinity between Arg558His MAD1 and MAD2 was –195.091 kJ/mol and that of the wild-type was –442.712 kJ/mol.
source: To assess this, we performed molecular dynamics simulations and found that the binding affinity between Arg558His MAD1 and MAD2 was –195.091 kJ/mol and that of the wild-type was –442.712 kJ/mol (Figure 7c).
evidence: Molecular dynamics simulation results shown in Figure 7c

claim: TPRN was identified as a novel significantly mutated gene in the XWLC cohort.
source: Notably, we identified TPRN as a novel significantly mutated gene in the XWLC cohort (Figure 7—figure supplement 1g and h)
evidence: Mutation analysis shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1g and h

claim: TPRN mutation status was associated with patients' outcomes.
source: Notably, we identified TPRN as a novel significantly mutated gene in the XWLC cohort (Figure 7—figure supplement 1g and h) whose status was also associated with patients' outcomes (Figure 7e).
evidence: Survival analysis shown in Figure 7e

claim: TPRN interacts with PPP1CA.
source: Previous studies have reported that TPRN interacts with PPP1CA (Ferrar et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Ferrar et al., 2012

claim: The binding affinities of the TPRN-PPP1CA complex were –694.372 kJ/mol and –877.570 kJ/mol in mutant and WT cases, respectively.

claim: CCK-8 assay showed significantly enhanced cell growth after transfection of the TPRN mutant allele in both A549 and H1299 cells.
source: CCK-8 assay showed significantly enhanced cell growth after transfection of the TPRN mutant allele in both A549 (Figure 7f) and H1299 cells (Figure 7—figure supplement 2a).
evidence: Experimental cell proliferation assay results shown in Figure 7f and Figure 7—figure supplement 2a

claim: The wound-healing assay showed that the TPRN mutant cell had achieved enhanced migration capacity.
source: Moreover, the wound-healing assay showed that the TPRN mutant cell had achieved enhanced migration capacity (Figure 7g–h and Figure 7—figure supplement 2b–c).
evidence: Experimental wound-healing assay results shown in Figure 7g-h and Figure 7—figure supplement 2b-c

claim: More cell clones were observed in TPRN His550Gln mutation cells in both TPRN-mutant A549 and H1299 cells.
source: Finally, more cell clones in TPRN His550Gln mutation cells were observed in both TPRN-mutant A549 and H1299 cells (Figure 7i).
evidence: Experimental colony formation assay results shown in Figure 7i

claim: TPRN His550Gln could be explored as a target in XWLC.
source: All these results supported that TPRN His550Gln could be explored as a target in XWLC.
evidence: Conclusion from molecular dynamics simulations and experimental validation
